result: The probe could not be evaluated: the step-600 policies sampled only 1 and 1 hack action(s) (seeds 0, 1) across 12,000 branches each, none in the held-out split, so AUROC is undefined.
notes: Reduced design because the shared machine was overloaded (load ~250 on 16 cores): 2 seeds (0, 1) instead of 3, 600 GRPO steps instead of 1,000, greedy eval every 50 steps on 1,000 held-out programs (seed 12345) instead of 2,000. SFT kept at the registered 1,000 steps x 256 because the most expensive SFT checkpoints were already cached and mixing SFT lengths would confound comparisons. Policy: 2-layer pre-LN transformer (4 heads, FFN 2d) over all 12 branches; SFT on the pilot demonstrator, GRPO 64 programs x 8 samples, lr 1e-3 (never reduced; no instability seen), KL 0.02 to the frozen SFT copy, grad-norm clip 1.0 as in the pilot. 'Final' means step 600. Std is over 2 seeds (ddof=1). runtime_s sums the wall time of the runs used (shared runs counted in each experiment), measured under heavy machine load. Features: final-layer (post-LN) hidden state at each broken position of the E31 visible-reward policy at step 600, standardised with seed 0's training statistics; L2 1e-3 logistic regression (LBFGS). Label: the action sampled from the policy at that branch is DELETE or STUB on an untested branch. 3,000 fixed programs shared by all seeds; first 2,250 for training, last 750 for every AUROC. Cross-seed test on seed 1 only (reduced from seeds 1 and 2). Verdict: supported if the seed-1 AUROC < 0.7 and in-seed > 0.95; refuted if seed-1 AUROC > 0.85. Verdict is mixed because neither the hypothesis nor the kill criterion can be evaluated: the visible-reward transformer did not hack (see E31), so there are no hacked branches to detect.
